title: Understanding Your Statement — The Balance on a Pre-Placement Statement, Patient Financial Account
content:
The balance printed on a pre-placement statement of the Patient Financial Account is the account's balance owed: every charge, reversed payment and refund posted to the account, less every payment, time-of-service collection and adjustment, with the remaining balance of an active or delinquent payment plan left off. Nothing else is left off the pre-placement statement; its balance is never below 0.00 and is rounded to the nearest cent once, at the end.

## What adds to the balance and what reduces it

| Adds to the balance owed | Reduces the balance owed |
|---|---|
| every charge posted (visits, deductible, coinsurance, non-covered services, fees) | every payment posted |
| every reversed payment (a returned check or ACH, a chargeback) | every time-of-service collection (copays and estimate collections) |
| every refund issued | every adjustment (discounts, write-offs, corrections) |

From the balance owed, the remaining balance of the patient's payment plan is left off when that plan is active or delinquent, as the Patient Payment Plans records show; a plan in any other status leaves nothing off.

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| charges posted | 1,240.00 |
| reversed payments | 95.00 |
| refunds issued | 0.00 |
| payments posted | 410.00 |
| time-of-service collections | 40.00 |
| adjustments | 185.00 |
| balance owed: 1,240.00 plus 95.00 plus 0.00, less 410.00, 40.00 and 185.00 | 700.00 |
| remaining balance of an active payment plan | 300.00 |
| statement balance: 700.00 less 300.00 | 400.00 |

Had the plan been paid off and closed, the statement balance would be the full 700.00; had payments and adjustments exceeded the charges, the statement balance would be 0.00.
